summary: Adds email search to the user index, update and destroy actions with routes, and a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.description: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the WHERE clause text. Any authenticated user controls that text. An authenticated user can inject SQL to read columns such as api_token or admin. That user can then take over admin accounts. Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.consequence: An authenticated user can inject SQL to read columns such as api_token or admin. That user can then take over admin accounts.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Destroy action exempt from admin check
findings.description: The change adds destroy to the require_admin exception list. The destroy action then deletes any user found by params[:id]. Any authenticated user can delete every other user, including admins. Remove destroy from the except list so the destroy action requires an admin.

findings.fix: Remove destroy from the except list so the destroy action requires an admin.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.description: The after_save callback runs on updates as well as creates. The callback also enqueues the mail before the transaction commits. Users receive a new welcome email whenever an admin updates them. A rolled back create still enqueues a welcome email. Use after_create_commit so the mail goes out once after a committed create.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.description: The change adds search, update, destroy and a mail callback. The repository contains no test that exercises any of them. Regressions in authorization and search reach production unnoticed. Add request tests for search, update and destroy, including the non-admin cases, and a model test for the callback.

candidate.message: Found an unscoped `find(...)` with user-controllable input. If the ActiveRecord model being searched against is sensitive, this may lead to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) behavior and allow users to read arbitrary records. Scope the find to the current user, e.g. `current_user.accounts.find(params[:id])`.

dropped.reason: The update action stays behind require_admin, so only admins can look up arbitrary users there. This directory app lets admins manage all users.
